title: tpg-world
label: Kris Adams

won.source: the fed's own End of an Era III (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-end-of-an-era-iii-2005-12-17.html)

how: Beat JC Sinn by pinfall in 9:56 at Madison Square Garden, finishing with a frog splash off the top rope under the Guerrero banner still hanging over the ramp.
note: Still champion at the record's own last word.

title: tpg-world
label: Chris Watts

won.source: PWE's own Revenge roster records, which give his greatest accomplishment as “Former TPG World Champion” and no date (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/the-new-revenge-roster-records-2005-05-31.html)

note: No date, no opponent and no title-change document survives for this reign; it is sequenced before Kris Adams's only because the record naming it predates his.

title: tpg-international
label: Wil The Thrill

won.source: PWE's own front page of 13 April 2005: “The Proving Grounds Superstar of the week: Wil The Thrill — Wil was able to retain his TPG International Championship in a main event match with Carlito Caribbean Cool!” (PWE's own front page as the board rendered it on 13 April 2005 (held in the workshop, not served))

note: Recorded as a retention; the win that started the reign is not in the record.

won.source: PWE's own Revenge roster records, which give his greatest accomplishment as “TPG International Champion” in the present tense while giving Wil the Thrill's in the past (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/the-new-revenge-roster-records-2005-05-31.html)

title: tpg-international
label: JC Sinn

won.source: the fed's own End of an Era III, which calls him “the International Champion” on the night he loses a World Championship match (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-end-of-an-era-iii-2005-12-17.html)

note: The fed's own commentary that night says both of the last two International Champions were crowned by tournaments and both went through David D on the way.

title: tpg-diva
label: So Cal Val

won.source: the fed's own End of an Era III (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-end-of-an-era-iii-2005-12-17.html)

how: Beat Trish Stratus by pinfall in 3:57 with a flapjack slam.

won.source: the fed's own commentary at End of an Era III: “That title has been around Stratus waist for as long as thee title has been created.” (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-end-of-an-era-iii-2005-12-17.html)
the fed's own ring announcer on TPG Uncensored, 9 October 2005: “Introducing the Women's Champion……..Laceeeeeeyyyyyyyy.” (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/tpg-uncensored-results-2005-10-10.html)

title: tpg-pride
label: AJ Styles

won.source: his own signature record, carried on a PWE roleplay of August 2004: “Pride Title (79 days - Lost it)” (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/iron-man-battle-royal-2004-08-16.html)

note: The length is the fed's own; the dates are not recoverable. One opponent's promo in the same thread has him lose the belt to Sabu — “you were also a holder of the TPG Pride title before losing it Sabu is my memory serves me correct” — which is hedged in its own sentence and is the only account of how the reign ended; recorded, not structured into a Sabu reign.

title: tpg-hardcore
label: Randy Walker

won.source: PWE's own Underground Network of 10 October 2005, where he leaves TPG still holding the belt (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/underground-network-oct-10-milw-wi-2005-10-09.html)

note: Carried out of the promotion rather than lost; the record does not say what became of the belt.

title: tpg-tag-team
label: The Patriots

won.source: PWE's own front page of 13 April 2005: “Mortis and Chaos were able to pick up a win over the former TPG Tag Team Champions - Joey Legend and Daniel Justice; The Patriots!” (PWE's own front page as the board rendered it on 13 April 2005 (held in the workshop, not served))

note: The record names them champions only in the past tense, in a news line about a match they were losing on another brand.

title: tpg-pride
label: Montel Vontavious Porter

won.source: the board's own results panel on its last surviving capture, which carries “TPG Showcase: Pride Title: Montel Vontavious Porter © d. The Mask” among the results of PWE's Trials 'N' Tribulations 2007 (the board's own last capture, 27 May 2007 (held in the workshop, not served))

note: Recorded as a retention: the belt is already his when the line is written, and the line is the last thing the record says about either the title or the promotion. Nothing survives of how or when he won it, and the belt had been described as dead since 2004.
